correctness.rationale: The beta-binomial success probability is a direct mixture of conditional binomial counts, with correct voting thresholds for either expert outcome. A coupling of adjacent direct-delegation strategies isolates two pivotal events, whose identical combinatorial prefactors produce an exact beta-function ratio. Gamma recurrence yields the stated finite product; a>b makes its factors >1 and a strictly monotone sign test. Harmonic-sum expansion for fixed a,b gives the unique positive limiting optimum fraction. The integer specialization telescopes to (k+3)/(k-r+1), producing an exact sharp count and tie classification. A standalone stdlib rational-arithmetic verifier passed 418 assertions on independent tail evaluations, marginal differences and selected full optimizer sets; finite checks do not substitute for the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Direct literature comparisons found the independent-signal bounded-optimum result already in Proposition 3 of arXiv:2306.03960 and the N=3 mixture-correlation extension in Appendix B.6.3 of arXiv:2212.09715; both are treated as prior art. Neither establishes the exact beta-mixture single-crossing ratio and positive limiting delegated share across arbitrary odd electorates. arXiv:2505.04136 addresses dependencies conceptually, but its inspected sections do not formulate this beta-mixture optimizer. arXiv:2608.16738 is close in theme but its available abstract describes a binary public common-signal framework and network delegation guarantees, and its full text was unavailable, leaving residual priority risk. Several targeted scientific-record and primary-literature searches did not identify dominating claims; negative searches alone are not proof of originality.

value.rationale: The precise mathematical gap is how epistemically optimal direct vote delegation scales with electorate size when the individual novice correctness events have common persistent dependence. Unlike the established O(1) independent benchmark, beta exchangeability produces a positive Θ(N) optimal delegated share, a structural separation with explicit dependence parameter and exact finite thresholds. It addresses the literature-motivated information loss versus expert weighting tradeoff, not an arbitrary small-n enumeration. The same marginal novice accuracy and expert accuracy can be held fixed across the two regimes; only dependence changes.
